cases.title: AI Mindmeld: specialist representations as latent inputs
cases.source_claim: Connector training maps frozen protein and molecule specialist embeddings into Gemma/Kimi internal states. README provides training, evaluation, inference code and public library; results are author-reported.
cases.ghostmesh_existing: GhostMesh plans multiple interchangeable inference backends and source-grounded tool communication; no qualified latent specialist interface.
cases.surprise: A specialist may convey features an LLM would never formulate as a text query.
cases.transfer: Future specialist-model experiments with an inspectable text-baseline and frozen-model isolated connector; no direct benefit to Scout web discovery.
cases.counterevidence: Learned connectors depend on specialist/backbone/extraction recipe, require training resources and complicate provenance; authors themselves flag reasoning failures.
cases.test: Produce an architecture and cost feasibility sheet for a single actual specialist task; benchmark text-only baseline first. No installs.

cases.title: devto-digest: deliberately search outside the interest bubble
cases.source_claim: A daily candidate pool feeds two sections, familiar followed tags and outside-followed-tag discovery; articles are rechecked before a weekly email. The repo describes editorial blurbs and escaping untrusted source content.
cases.ghostmesh_existing: Scout discovers via tracked topics and sources with metadata relevance and source revision receipts.
cases.surprise: The deliberate outside-interest cohort creates discovery opportunities that topic relevance ranking tends to erase.
cases.transfer: Add an opt-in private 'outside current interests' sample with no popularity threshold and without filtering unconventional sources out.
cases.counterevidence: DEV engagement scoring rewards popularity, not originality; personalized follows require private API access, and their user-specific preferences cannot be inferred from public data.
cases.test: On a frozen 59-lead Scout snapshot, partition source/topic familiarity versus outside-bubble candidates, retain low-scoring examples and assess actual surprise with human review.

cases.title: Unpile: local attention triage with explicit lost-value metrics
cases.source_claim: README describes on-device TabPFN keep/skim/drop prediction, local Gemma writing, deterministic fallback, and held-out scoring that tracks desirable articles mistakenly dropped.
cases.ghostmesh_existing: Scout keeps unreviewed sources and uses keyword triage, but its rank quality and false-negative costs are not calibrated.
cases.surprise: Measuring interesting discoveries lost by a filter may matter more than optimizing the number shown in the reading queue.
cases.transfer: Shadow-score existing Scout leads without removing any, record human keep/discard labels and count missed surprising items before any automated suppression.
cases.counterevidence: Article examples and efficiency metrics are author-reported, and predicting personal read-later behavior differs from discovering breakthrough ideas; dropping sources would be unacceptable before calibration.
cases.test: Use a frozen, consented subset of 40 source leads, compare metadata-only review against shadow triage, explicitly count false negatives and retain every original record.
